questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{9}{{x}^{2}-6}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{9}{{x}^{2}-6} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{9}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{9}{{x}^{2}})}{(1-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{0}{1-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$

questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{12x-3{x}^{4}}{3{x}^{2}+7}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{12x-3{x}^{4}}{3{x}^{2}+7} \\  & {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{3{x}^{4}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12}{x}-3{x}^{2})}{(3+\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{0-3{x}^{2}}{3+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(-{x}^{2}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{9{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-x}{5{x}^{2}+3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{9{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-x}{5{x}^{2}+3} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{9{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{5{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(9x+1-\frac{1}{x})}{(5+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(9x+1-0)}{(5+0)} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(9x+1) \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{{x}^{5}+5x+3}{{x}^{4}-2} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{5x}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(x+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{4}})}{(1-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\text{ }\frac{x+0+0}{1-0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,x \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
